LMGTE.title: Proton wins in the rain as Silverstone is cut short
LMGTE.dek: Ried, Roda and Tandy took Proton’s Porsche to the GTE win a lap clear of the RAM Racing Ferraris when the weather ended the 2013 opener after 48 laps.

chapters.title: A new-look GTE class
text: The opening round of the revived European Le Mans Series came with a GTE class built almost from scratch. The ACO had restricted it to GTE Am rules, with cars at least a year old and a gentleman driver in every crew, and the result was a far healthier field than the thin grids of 2012: five Ferrari 458 Italias against three Porsche 911 GT3 RSRs. Races had also been cut from six hours to three, and the series now shared its weekend with the FIA World Endurance Championship.

RAM Racing, a Silverstone-based newcomer, ran the #52 for Mowlem and Griffin and the #53 for Jeanette and Montecalvo, after being forced to convert its brand-new 2013 Ferraris back to 2012 specification. JMW Motorsport, reigning GTE champions, had signed Ferrari factory driver Bertolini only days earlier to share the #66 with Camathias. AF Corse fielded two cars, the #54 and the #55, the latter with Perazzini, Cioci and Leo. On the Porsche side Proton ran Ried, Roda and Tandy in the #77, Prospeed entered the #75 for Perrodo, Collard and Crubilé, and IMSA Performance Matmut paired Milesi with Henzler in the #67.

Friday was cold and wet. Griffin headed GTE in the opening session by 4.5 seconds, mentioning a misfire that went away after changes, and he said GTE cars were closer to the prototypes in such conditions. In the second session, as the track dried, Tandy went straight to the top in the Proton Porsche with a 2:03.454, Griffin 0.65 seconds behind and Collard third.

chapters.title: Mowlem gives RAM a first pole
text: The GT cars ran first, in a 20-minute session on a track that was still far from grippy. Mowlem was first out in the #52. Tandy beat the first benchmark by a second, Mowlem answered with a 2:03.114, and a late 2:02.358 put the Ferrari on pole.

Tandy improved in the closing minutes to 2:02.653, three tenths short, and the Prospeed Porsche took third with 2:02.685; Perrodo had been given extra time in the car because he had missed the dry running in practice. AF Corse’s #55 was fourth on 2:02.731 and JMW’s #66 fifth on 2:03.015, with the second RAM car, the #53, on 2:04.412, the #54 on 2:05.198 and Milesi’s #67 on 2:08.745. Mowlem said he had pushed every lap and been on for a 2:01 before traffic intervened. It was RAM’s first pole in the series, in its first qualifying session.

chapters.title: Rain on the formation lap
text: Everyone started on slicks, and the rain arrived during the formation laps. Those who headed straight to the pits for wet tyres were back out before the safety car was officially deployed, and the new ELMS rule that keeps the pit lane closed for the first three safety-car laps punished the rest. Montecalvo had made the early stop and led GTE through much of the opening hour in the #53. Tandy changed to normal wets at the right moment, then to full wets perhaps a lap late by his own reckoning, and still held a lap lead; by the end of the hour the Proton Porsche headed the class.

chapters.title: Tandy spins and keeps the lead
text: Tandy was still in front as the second hour began, and kept the lead through a spin and light contact with Milesi’s IMSA Performance Porsche at Copse. He said the car aquaplaned into the other Porsche and that he went to apologise as soon as he got out. Proton also had a clock to watch: Tandy needed to stop before the 90-minute mark to avoid breaching his driving-time limit, and the safety car’s return, which closed the pit lane for three laps, made that a dilemma. Mowlem, who had completed his stint, suggested stopping the race at 70 per cent distance.

chapters.title: Stopped at 75 per cent
text: The rain never eased, and the race was brought to an end after 2 hours 15 minutes and 48 laps. With 75 per cent of the three-hour distance run, full points were awarded and no restart was attempted. Proton’s Porsche took the class win on the lead lap, fifth overall, with the RAM Ferraris of Mowlem and Griffin and of Jeanette and Montecalvo, and JMW’s Ferrari, all one lap down behind it.

chapters.title: Proton wins ahead of RAM
text: Ried, Roda and Tandy won the class in the #77 with 48 laps, a lap clear of the field. The RAM Racing #52 of Mowlem and Griffin was second, ahead of its sister #53 and the JMW #66, all on 47 laps. Prospeed’s #75 was fifth with 46, IMSA Performance’s #67 was four laps down, and AF Corse’s #55 and #54 completed 43 and 42. All eight GTE cars were classified. Tandy’s 2:17.006 was the quickest class lap.
Tandy said Michelin wets suited the Porsche in changing conditions. RAM went on to win the GTE title that year, and the series moved on to Imola on 18 May.

facts.t: RAM on pole at first attempt
facts.v: Mowlem’s 2:02.358 gave RAM Racing pole in the team’s first qualifying session in the series, three tenths clear of Tandy’s Proton Porsche.

facts.t: Pit lane shut for three laps
facts.v: A new ELMS regulation kept the pit lane closed for the first three laps of a safety-car period, which cost the cars that had stayed out on slicks.
The race ran 2:15:22 and 48 laps before being abandoned; 75 per cent of the three-hour distance was enough for full points.
Mowlem and Griffin went on to win the 2013 LMGTE title after Proton’s win at Silverstone.

GTC.title: AF Corse Ferrari takes GTC at rain-hit Silverstone
GTC.dek: Rizzoli, Gai and Casè took the AF Corse Ferrari to the GTC win, 46 laps and 13th overall, when rain stopped the opener after 2h15.

chapters.title: A new class for GT3 cars
text: GTC was new to the European Le Mans Series in 2013, a class for GT3-based cars running to an ELMS-specific balance of performance rather than the SRO one. Five cars were expected over the season: two Autorlando Porsches, an AF Corse Ferrari, a MOMO Megatron DF1 Audi R8 LMS Ultra and an Ecurie Ecosse BMW Z4. The BMW team had been drawn from the Blancpain Endurance Series by a package that included an automatic Le Mans 2014 entry in GTE for the GTC class winner.

At Silverstone the AF Corse Ferrari was the only car of its make in the class, driven by Rizzoli, Gai and Casè. The first wet session showed how different GTC was from GTE: the GT3 cars were around eight seconds quicker in the worst of the rain, which Griffin of RAM Racing put down to ABS, softer set-ups and less aquaplaning. The Audi of Derdaele set mid-2:20s early on, and as conditions improved Rizzoli topped the class with 2:21.939. In the second session the Ecosse BMW was quickest at the finish, Smith setting 2:05.543.

chapters.title: Audi quickest despite a puncture
text: GTC qualified with the GTE cars in the first session. The Ecosse BMW came straight back in after one lap for tyres, and Smith’s 2:03.737 first led the class. Giermaziak, the last of the GT cars to set a time, then put the Audi top of GTC with 2:03.484 from a single flying lap, and said afterwards he had suffered lock-ups caused by a right-front puncture. Casè spun the AF Corse Ferrari on the damp track, and its best was 2:04.233, behind both the Audi and the BMW. Giermaziak said he expected at least six GTC cars at Imola.

chapters.title: Slicks or wets
text: The rain that fell during the formation laps hit GTC as hard as the other classes. Smith said the Ecosse BMW had started on slicks and then pitted at once for wets, and by the time it caught the Audi it was a lap ahead. Later Smith lost time through contact at Abbey with a LMPC car and ran second for a while; the AF Corse Ferrari had a troubled spell with Gai at the wheel. Derdaele took the Audi off at Stowe, and that incident brought the safety car back out.

chapters.title: Audi on a flatbed
text: The safety car was out again as the second hour went on and closed the pit lane for three laps, but cars kept sliding off on the wet grass. Derdaele had said every lap felt different, and Bader, taking over the Audi, hit the barriers hard enough to add to the rear damage and the car left the circuit on a flatbed.

chapters.title: Called off after 48 laps
text: The rain did not ease and the race was stopped after 2 hours 15 minutes, with 75 per cent of the scheduled distance run and full points awarded. The AF Corse Ferrari took the flag on 46 laps, 13th overall.

chapters.title: Ferrari takes the class
text: Rizzoli, Gai and Casè took the GTC win in the AF Corse Ferrari, 13th overall on 46 laps, and Casè’s 2:23.579 on lap 15 was the quickest GTC lap of the race. The Audi’s race had ended on the back of a flatbed after Bader’s accident.
The next round was at Imola on 18 May, where Giermaziak expected at least six GTC cars.

facts.t: GT3 cars romp in the wet
facts.v: In the opening wet practice the GTC cars were about eight seconds faster than GTE, which Griffin put down to ABS, softer set-ups and less aquaplaning.
Giermaziak’s 2:03.484 was the best GTC time from a single flying lap, set with a right-front puncture.

facts.t: Le Mans prize for the class winner
facts.v: The GTC package included an automatic GTE entry to the 2014 Le Mans 24 Hours for the class-winning team.
